descriptions.BENBUSI112: Accounting & Corporate Finance introduces financial and management accounting, financial-statement preparation and analysis, costing, pricing, budgeting and organisational control. Students assess investment decisions using accounting measures, discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return and cost of capital. A case study examines the misuse of an accounting principle and its effects on financial statements.
descriptions.BENBUSI211: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.
descriptions.BENBUSI311: Transnational Business Law studies legal frameworks for cross-border business, including contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce. Comparative and international perspectives support analysis of legal risks through discussions, problem-based assignments and an arbitration simulation.
descriptions.BENBUSI312: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.
descriptions.BENECON111: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
descriptions.BENECON211: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
descriptions.BENECON212: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
descriptions.BENECON311: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
descriptions.BENECON312: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
descriptions.BENECON314: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
descriptions.BENENTR111: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
descriptions.BENENTR211: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.
descriptions.BENENTR212: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
descriptions.BENENTR311: Market Research explores how companies learn about customer preferences. Students plan and carry out research, analyse their findings and present how those findings can inform business decisions.
descriptions.BENENTR312: Examines how trade, globalisation and political, cultural and technological conditions shape international business decisions. Students analyse governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate a business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices.
descriptions.BENGATE101: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
descriptions.BENGATE102: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.
descriptions.BENLEAD111: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.
descriptions.BENLEAD112: Studies leadership communication through theory, persuasion, emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Students analyse literary characters, film and speeches, interview a leader, prepare a communication advisory report, and develop an address explaining their own ethical leadership vision.
descriptions.BENLEAD211: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.
descriptions.BENLEAD311: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.
descriptions.BENLEAD312: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.
